verses.1: My son, guard my words; treasure my commandments within you.
verses.2: Guard my commandments, and you will live; keep my teaching as the apple of your eye.
verses.3: Tie them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
verses.4: Say to Wisdom, "You are my sister," and to Understanding, "You are my intimate."
verses.5: To guard you from a foreign woman, from the smooth-tongued outsider.
verses.6: For I saw through the window of my house, from the lattice within,
verses.7: a naive young man, lacking sense,
verses.8: passing by the corner of the street, near her door, along the paths of her house,
verses.9: in the late evening, in the hush of the night and darkness,
verses.10: when suddenly a woman meets him, her face like a prostitute, her eyes a trap.
verses.11: She is restless and wanton; her feet do not rest in her house;
verses.12: sometimes she is out in the streets, sometimes in the public squares, lying in wait at every corner.
verses.13: She grabs him and kisses him; she flirts with him and says,
verses.14: "I have peace offerings today. I have fulfilled my vows."
verses.15: "That is why I came out to meet you, to look for your face and to find you."
verses.16: I have spread my bed with coverlets from Egypt, with fine linen and embroidered tapestries.
verses.17: I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, with incense and cinnamon.
verses.18: Come, let us drink sweet wine, until we find love at dawn.
verses.19: For the man is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
verses.20: He has taken a silver cord in his hand; he will return to his house in the days of the feast.
verses.21: She seduces him with much flattery, and with the words of her mouth she draws him in.
verses.22: He follows her suddenly, like a bull toward slaughter, like a wild donkey toward the bridle.
verses.23: Until the arrow strikes his liver, like a swift bird toward the trap, not knowing that it is for his life.
verses.24: Now then, you children, listen to me and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
verses.25: Let your heart not incline to her ways, do not wander in her paths.
verses.26: For she has struck down many, and all her slain are strong.
verses.27: Her ways lead to Sheol; her paths descend to the chambers of death.

notes:
Notes
- v. 20: "days of the feast" is a plausible interpretation of the Hebrew, which is somewhat ambiguous. The Septuagint reads "in the days of many" but "days of the feast" fits the context better.
- v. 22: "wild donkey toward the bridle" is a fresh rendering of the Hebrew metaphor, which uses a term that can mean "wild donkey" or "foolish one." The latter might be more literal, but the former is more evocative in English.
